changedBeliefs: After [exp 195](195-stmt-cache-name-tokens.md), [exp 198](198-direct-buf-int-float-json.md), and [exp 199](199-row-level-buf-ensure.md) had collapsed the per-cell formatter, column-name token, and `buf_ensure` work inside `write_json_to_buf`, the remaining per-cell cost was the SQLite API itself: every `sqlite3_column_*` call runs a fresh `columnMem` lookup (mutex enter/leave + result-row range check, all no-op on the NOMUTEX connections resqlite opens but still function calls) plus `columnMallocFailure` (mutex leave + `sqlite3ApiExit`). Two-three of those fire per cell — `sqlite3_column_type` + `sqlite3_column_int64/double` for INT/FLOAT, `sqlite3_column_type` + `sqlite3_column_text/blob` + `sqlite3_column_bytes` for TEXT/BLOB.

Hoisting `sqlite3_column_value(stmt, i)` to the top of the per-cell switch and dispatching through `sqlite3_value_type` / `sqlite3_value_int64` / `sqlite3_value_double` / `sqlite3_value_text` / `sqlite3_value_bytes` / `sqlite3_value_blob` collapses those 2-3 `columnMem` lookups into one. The SQLite amalgamation literally defines `sqlite3_column_*` as `sqlite3_value_* ∘ columnMem`, so the output is bit-identical. The `unprotected sqlite3_value` warning the SQLite docs attach to `sqlite3_column_value` does not apply: it targets multithreaded races, and resqlite opens every connection with SQLITE_OPEN_NOMUTEX and dedicates each connection to a single isolate worker.

Two order-flipped focused passes reproduce a same-direction candidate-faster effect on every shape. select_bytes_int_heavy.dart: 10k×8 small ints -0.9%/-2.1%, 10k×20 small ints -2.4%/-1.9%, 10k×20 big ints -3.4%/-0.5%, mixed -1.7%/-1.6%, 1k×2 ints -4.7%/-2.9%. select_bytes_real_int_fastpath.dart: 10k×8 integral reals -3.1%/-3.5%, 10k×20 integral reals -6.1%/-6.1%, fractional-REAL guard -1.0%/-0.4% (snprintf dominates), mixed -1.1%/-1.2%, 1k×2 integral reals -4.4%/-2.7%. select_bytes_wide_cols.dart: 10k×20 int -3.5%/-6.1%, 10k×8 mixed -5.0%/-3.4%, 10k×20 mixed -3.2%/-2.6%. large_bytes_transfer.dart: large TEXT -2.0%/-3.1%, small TEXT -3.8%/-3.7%.

The fractional-REAL guard staying inside ±1% across both passes is the cleanest evidence the saving is columnMem amortization rather than noise — `snprintf("%.17g")` dominates per-cell wall on that lane, so an experiment that genuinely only saves per-cell FFI lookup cost should not move it.
nextSignals: The same `sqlite3_column_value` → `sqlite3_value_*` pattern is mechanically applicable to `resqlite_step_row` and `resqlite_step_row_hash` (the rows / stream-hash paths). It should not be folded into this experiment because the load-bearing harnesses differ — `select_maps`, `row_map_facade`, and `single_stream_long_payload_hash` — and the per-cell FFI saving is a smaller fraction of total wall there (each cell pays Dart-side decode and isolate transfer afterwards). Pick it up as its own experiment with the right gate.

After exp 203 the remaining per-cell SQLite cost in `write_json_to_buf` is the one `columnMem` invocation inside `sqlite3_column_value` itself. The only ways below that are a per-statement type cache that skips the value lookup entirely for cells whose type can be predicted (exp 200's storage-class-stable moonshot rejected this on hidden-default semantics) or a SQLite-internal API resqlite does not expose.

Any future per-cell encoder change in this file should keep the hoisted `sqlite3_value*` pattern intact: it has no per-cell cost above the SQLite-API floor and exposes the cell as a single pointer that subsequent micro-optimizations (per-cell type prediction, value-prefix templates) can dispatch off without re-introducing the `column_*` lookup chain.
